MOVE below 80 is calm, 80-120 is moderate uncertainty, and 150+ is high stress; 100.20 is moderate. SOFR measures secured overnight funding, not unsecured bank funding. NFCI below zero indicates looser-than-average broad financial conditions; -0.487 is the latest returned weekly observation for Oct 23, not a live reading.

Fed & Policy Watch
  • The Federal Reserve Board calendar lists no FOMC decision this week; it schedules minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting for Wed Nov 18 at 2:00 PM ET.
  • Selected Fed statistical releases this week: H.15 Wed Nov 4 at 4:15 PM ET, H.4.1 Thu Nov 5 at 4:30 PM ET and H.8 Fri Nov 6 at 4:15 PM ET, each according to its own Board-calendar day list. Chicago Fed NFCI publication is set for Wed Nov 4 at 8:30 AM ET for the week ending Oct 30.
  • Latest funding/conditions readings are lagged: SOFR 3.94% effective Oct 29, NFCI -0.487 for the week ending Oct 23, MOVE 100.20 (moderate) and the official 10-year Treasury close at 4.94%. These are context indicators, not live funding or rate quotes.
Omissions and Watch
  • Date/event conflict check: Census confirms Construction Spending for Sep on Nov 2 at 10:00 AM and Manufacturers' Shipments, Inventories and Orders for Sep on Nov 3 at 10:00 AM, aligning with New York Fed dates/times. On Nov 4 at 8:30 AM the Census annual calendar names U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services for Sep; the New York Fed calendar separately labels Advance International Trade in Goods and Trade balance at that time. Kept the New York Fed event names; the exact Census/New York Fed title correspondence is not resolved.
  • BEA schedules GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits for Q3 2026 on Nov 25 at 8:30 AM and Personal Income and Outlays for Oct 2026 on Dec 2 at 8:30 AM. The New York Fed November calendar also lists Personal Income and the PCE Deflator on Nov 25 at 8:30 AM without a period. That period/date conflict is unresolved; listed the New York Fed event as named with period not stated and separately retained BEA's verified Oct release on Dec 2. Do not assume they are the same release. BLS.gov was not requested; New York Fed calendars are the cited BLS release date/time source. New York Fed dates/times are tentative and subject to change.
  • Energy schedule check: EIA petroleum lists the standard Wednesday release, so Nov 4 at 10:30 AM is included, as is its Nov 12 noon Veterans Day exception for data through Nov 6. EIA natural gas lists the standard Thursday 10:30 AM release, so Nov 5 is included, and a Nov 13 10:30 AM Veterans Day exception. This corrects the prior briefing's missing standard Nov 4/Nov 5 reports and Nov 12/13 treatment.
  • Philadelphia Fed's own MBOS release calendar confirms the November survey on Thu Nov 19 at 8:30 AM, not Nov 5 as in the prior briefing; the corrected Nov 19 event is listed. TreasuryDirect verifies competitive bill bid-close times for the 13- and 26-week bills on Nov 2 and the 6-week bill on Nov 3. Upcoming Treasury records with no competitive close time are omitted from the timed calendar.
  • Routine Fed CP releases and other non-material statistical rows are omitted; this is a selected calendar, not exhaustive. No verified unscheduled geopolitical or policy watch item from this run; this is not a full risk review. No exchange-specific market-structure event or product-hours verification was available.
  • Sources checked: New York Fed November and December Economic Indicators Calendars; Federal Reserve Board November calendar, FOMC calendar and H.4.1; Census 2026 Economic Indicator Calendar; BEA news schedule; Chicago Fed release calendar and NFCI observations; Philadelphia Fed MBOS release calendar; TreasuryDirect; EIA petroleum and natural gas schedules; New York Fed SOFR; U.S. Treasury daily yield curve; Yahoo Finance charts. Reconfirm live event/auction updates, market depth, trading hours and selected contract before execution.
Trading Strategy Note | ES Futures
BASE CASE
Friday SPY fell 1.77%, while ES=F is 0.54% above Friday's completed daily bar in the early Monday quote. The official 10Y close eased 4 bp to 4.94%; MOVE rose to 100.20, still in the moderate-uncertainty band, and VIX closed at 19.42. Today's 10:00 AM Construction and ISM Manufacturing releases are the first scheduled catalysts, followed by bill auctions. Treat early price discovery as event-sensitive; wait for live rates, volatility and liquidity confirmation. Scenario framing only, not a trade signal.
INVALIDATION
Reassess if ES loses its early overnight strength without confirmation from Treasury yields, volatility or market depth; if scheduled data materially reprices rates; or if the selected contract's hours or liquidity differ. No unsupported levels or targets are supplied. Verify contract, event updates and fresh quotes before execution.
